Canon's integrated-grip professional RF bodies; both described in Canon's specification tables with a full-frame back-illuminated stacked CMOS sensor and a body over 1 kg with battery and card.

Nikon states the same sensor (35.9 x 23.9 mm CMOS, 45.7 effective megapixels), the same 493 focus points and the same 8K UHD 30p maximum video mode for both.
Nikon's heritage-styled Z bodies; grouped by design line only — the Zf is FX (35.9 x 23.9 mm) and the Zfc is DX (23.5 x 15.7 mm), so this is not a generational relationship.
Nikon states the same DX sensor (23.5 x 15.7 mm CMOS, 20.9 effective megapixels) and the same EN-EL25a battery for both.

Sony states the same sensor for both: APS-C (23.3 x 15.5 mm) Exmor R CMOS, max. approx. 26 million effective pixels for stills and 19.9 million for video.

Same maker, same sensor format and the same stated effective pixel count: Canon gives both as APS-C at approx. 32.5 effective megapixels (90D approx. 22.3 x 14.8 mm; R7 approx. 22.3 x 14.8 mm). The 90D is the EF-S DSLR, the R7 the RF-mount mirrorless body at that resolution.
Same maker, same sensor format (full-frame), same segment — Canon's smaller full-frame body without in-body stabilisation, in the EF and RF generations respectively.
Same maker, same APS-C format, same entry segment: Canon gives both as approx. 22.3 x 14.9 mm at 24.1-24.2 effective megapixels, the 250D as an EF-S DSLR and the R50 as its RF-mount counterpart.
Same maker, same sensor format and effective pixel count: Nikon states 35.9 x 23.9 mm CMOS at 24.5 effective megapixels for both, the D780 on the F mount and the Z6III on the Z mount.

Sony states the same sensor description and the same 33 effective megapixels for both (35.9 x 23.9 mm Exmor R CMOS); the 7C II is the smaller package at 514 g against 658 g, with a 0.39-type 2,359,296-dot viewfinder against the 7 IV's 0.5-type 3,686,400-dot unit.

Both Sony full-frame E-mount bodies of the same generation; Sony states 12.1 effective megapixels and an ISO 80-102400 range for the 7S III against 33 effective megapixels and ISO 100-51200 for the 7 IV — the same format traded for sensitivity against resolution.

Canon states the same RF mount and the same full-frame format for both, at approx. 45.0 effective megapixels (R5) against approx. 20.1 (R6), with the R5 taking CFexpress plus SD and the R6 two SD slots.

Nikon states the same sensor, focus-point count and maximum video mode for both; the Z9 is the integrated-grip EN-EL18d body at 1340 g and 149 x 149.5 x 90.5 mm, the Z8 the EN-EL15c body at 910 g and 144 x 118.5 x 83 mm.

Fujifilm states the same sensor and processor for both (X-Trans CMOS 5 HR, 40.2 MP, X-Processor 5); the X-H2 adds a CFexpress Type B slot and an 8K video mode and weighs 660 g against the X-T5's 557 g.

Same sensor format and closely matching stated resolution: Canon gives approx. 45.0 effective megapixels on a 36.0 x 24.0 mm sensor, Nikon 45.7 million on 35.9 x 23.9 mm. Both are full-frame mirrorless bodies with a CFexpress card slot. No succession or equivalence beyond format and resolution is implied.

Same sensor format and segment: both are the maker's stacked-sensor full-frame flagship without an integrated grip — Canon states a "full-frame back-illuminated stacked CMOS sensor" and Sony an "Exmor RS CMOS" 35.9 x 24.0 mm sensor.
Same sensor format and same body class: both are full-frame integrated-grip professional bodies, Canon at 157.6 x 149.5 x 87.3 mm and 1115 g, Nikon at 149 x 149.5 x 90.5 mm and 1340 g.
Same sensor format and closely matching stated resolution: Canon approx. 24.1 effective megapixels on a full-frame stacked sensor, Sony approx. 24.6 million on a 35.6 x 23.8 mm Exmor RS sensor.

Same sensor format and matching stated resolution: Canon approx. 24.2 effective megapixels on 36.0 x 24.0 mm, Nikon 24.5 million on 35.9 x 23.9 mm; both are the maker's mid-range full-frame mirrorless body with in-body stabilisation.

Same sensor format: Nikon 24.5 million effective pixels on 35.9 x 23.9 mm, Sony 33 million on 35.9 x 23.9 mm; both are the maker's full-frame all-rounder with in-body stabilisation and SD-only storage on the Nikon side.

Same sensor format (APS-C) and same segment — the maker's fastest APS-C body — though the sensors differ in stated size: Canon approx. 22.3 x 14.8 mm at 32.5 MP, Fujifilm 23.5 x 15.6 mm at 26.16 MP. See the APS-C crop-factor technology entry for why those areas are not the same.
Same sensor format (APS-C) and same enthusiast segment; Canon states approx. 22.3 x 14.9 mm at 24.2 MP, Sony 23.3 x 15.5 mm at approx. 26 MP.
Same sensor format (APS-C) and same segment; Nikon states 23.5 x 15.7 mm at 20.9 MP, Canon approx. 22.3 x 14.9 mm at 24.2 MP.

Same sensor format (APS-C) and same segment — both are the maker's viewfinder-less, video-first interchangeable-lens body; Sony's table lists the viewfinder as "-" and Nikon's specification lists none.
Same sensor format (APS-C) and closely matching stated resolution: Fujifilm 26.1 million effective pixels on 23.5 x 15.6 mm, Sony approx. 26 million on 23.3 x 15.5 mm.
